 Umno calls for explanation over declassification of Najib's pardons board meeting minutes
 By BENJAMIN LEE 
 Wednesday, 18 Nov 2026
 | 5:35 PM MYT

 PETALING JAYA: Umno has called for an official explanation over the alleged declassification of minutes from the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon.
 Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said questioned whether the minutes had been officially declassified, and if so, when the decision was made and who authorised it.
 ALSO READ: Alleged declassified minutes on Najib’s house arrest shared on social media 
 She said the proposal to declassify the minutes had not yet been raised in the Cabinet meeting on Nov 13, and that the process was being arranged, taking into account legal requirements.
 She then asked whether the government would officially reclassify the documents.
 "The decision to reclassify documents must be made by the authorised party under Section 2C of the Official Secrets Act 1972, in accordance with the applicable procedures.
 “As such, the relevant authorities must clarify if the minutes have been officially reclassified. If so, when was the decision made and who made it?
 “They must also explain if the reclassification covers the entire minutes, including related attachments, or only certain portions," she said in a press statement on Wednesday (Nov 18).
 Azalina said the authorities must also clarify the legal basis, procedures and purpose behind any reclassification of the minutes.
 She added that transparency in handling Pardons Board records must be accompanied by compliance with the law.
 "Umno respects the position of the Pardons Board and upholds the pardon powers of His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong as provided for under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution," she added.
 This comes after former Damansara MP Tony Pua shared several pages of the alleged minutes on social media on Wednesday (Nov 18), claiming they had been declassified.
 Pua claimed the minutes showed that the Attorney General and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh had opposed allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
